live.name: NICKEL FOXCROFT
live.headline: NICKEL FOXCROFT: a threat actor known by many names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists NICKEL FOXCROFT under many aliases, including APT37 and ScarCruft, and names eight tools tied to it. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: NICKEL FOXCROFT is the Secureworks name for a threat actor tracked under many other names.
Its aliases include APT37, ATK4, Group 123, InkySquid, Moldy Pisces, Operation Daybreak, Operaton Erebus, RICOCHET CHOLLIMA, Reaper, ScarCruft, TA-RedAnt and Venus 121.
The catalogue links eight tools to the actor: Bluelight, Chinotto, GOLDBACKDOOR, KevDroid, KoSpy, PoorWeb, ROKRAT and final1stpy.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: NICKEL FOXCROFT
next.headline: NICKEL FOXCROFT (APT37, ScarCruft): a long-running Korean-focused espionage group
next.in_short: Vendors describe NICKEL FOXCROFT, also tracked as APT37 and ScarCruft, as a North Korea-linked espionage actor. It mainly targets South Korea and people tied to North Korea, using phishing, cloud-based backdoors and Android spyware.

sentences.t: Secureworks tracks the group as NICKEL FOXCROFT. Other names in the catalogue include APT37, ScarCruft, Reaper, InkySquid, Group 123, Venus 121 and RICOCHET CHOLLIMA.
CrowdStrike describes RICOCHET CHOLLIMA as a DPRK-nexus targeted intrusion adversary that has run espionage operations since at least 2016.
ESET says ScarCruft, also known as APT37 or Reaper, has operated since at least 2012 and is suspected to be a North Korean espionage group.

Lookout calls ScarCruft a North Korean state-sponsored group. It attributes the KoSpy Android spyware to APT37 with medium confidence, and notes that North Korean groups share infrastructure and techniques, which makes attribution harder.
CrowdStrike says observed operations have almost exclusively targeted the Republic of Korea. It assesses the focus to be government officials, NGOs, academics and journalists.
Genians reported a March 2025 spear phishing campaign by APT37 against activists focused on North Korea.
ESET infers that the main targets of a game-platform attack were ethnic Koreans in Yanbian, China, most likely refugees or defectors.
Kudelski Security and Sekoia say the related cluster Reaper focuses on North Korean defectors, South Korean activists and NGOs.
One analysis of the RokRat backdoor describes phishing emails with ZIP files that hide shortcut (LNK) files. These start a multi-stage chain that loads the payload in memory.
RokRat uses the cloud services pCloud, Yandex and Dropbox for command and control. It can capture screenshots, run commands and collect files.

AhnLab's ASEC, as reported in the press, linked APT37 to phishing attacks from January 2023. These exploited an old Hangul word processor flaw, CVE-2017-8291, and delivered a backdoor called M2RAT that hid its payload in an image.
Lookout describes KoSpy as Android spyware disguised as utility apps and distributed through Google Play and Firebase Firestore. Samples date from March 2022 to March 2024.
Genians says the actor uses NordVPN and AstrillVPN to hide its network origin.
Genians reported Operation ToyBox Story in March 2025. Lures imitated an event from a South Korean national security think tank and delivered the RoKRAT malware.
ESET reports that ScarCruft trojanized Windows and Android parts of a video game platform for Yanbian. It says the attack was probably under way since late 2024 and delivered the BirdCall backdoor.
Zscaler ThreatLabz describes a campaign called Ruby Jumper, published in February 2026. It spreads through removable media to reach air-gapped networks.
Zscaler also documented infection chains using a shortcut or Windows help file lure. They deliver the Rustonotto and Chinotto backdoors, then the FadeStealer data-theft tool.
Treat unexpected ZIP, shortcut and help-file attachments with caution, especially if you work with North Korea-related issues.
Be wary of utility apps from unfamiliar publishers, and check removable media before using it on isolated networks.
